$comment: Pinned scan-surface baseline for the column-type-imports guard (#1769).
The guard counts how many files it scans per extension and FAILS if any
count drops below the floor pinned here. This closes Hole 1: moving a
code extension (like .tsx) from SCANNED_EXTENSIONS into
NON_CODE_EXTENSIONS silently disables its analysis, and the guard used
to announce [OK] with a smaller count. Now a drop fails loudly, naming
the extension and the gap.
Lower a floor deliberately when files are legitimately removed from the
tree (e.g. a .tsx page is deleted). Never raise a floor without review
— that would mask a silent surface reduction. To lower a floor: edit the
count, commit, and let CI verify the new floor matches the tree.
Per-extension floors (not a total) so the message names the exact
extension that shrank. Extensions with 0 files have floor 0 — they are
protected by CORE_EXTENSIONS (cannot be declared non-code) and by the
"still scanned" test, not by the ratchet.
R7: the three mutable sets below are pinned here so that ANY change to
SCANNED_EXTENSIONS, NON_CODE_EXTENSIONS, or EXEMPT_FILES fails the guard
loudly. This closes the three bypasses the r6 reviewer found:
- Hole 1 (exemptions): adding a path to isExempt silently hides a file.
- Hole 2 (justification): a 24-char string of 'a' passes the length bar.
- Hole 3 (extension relocation): .ctsx/.mjs/.cjs have floor 0, so
moving them to non-code keeps the real-tree guard green.
The pin makes every one of these gestures visible: the guard compares the
runtime set against the pinned baseline and fails on any divergence.
R8 (round 2 #1943): the floors EQUAL the live tree — the guard itself
refuses any other value (assertFloorsPinned). Note: walk() does NOT exclude
test files; they are part of the scanned surface. On 2026-08-31, after this
branch merged develop (which added two .ts files), the live tree holds
.ts:300 and .tsx:498, and the floors were moved to match in that same
merge — which is the mechanism working: a floor moves in the commit that
moves the tree. The
floors were raised in this same PR to match the live counts: floors may
only be raised to match verified live counts, never lowered to mask a
regression. Raising floors in the same PR that adds the files is the
correct workflow — a future tightening PR can further raise them if the
minimal-slack blind spot becomes a concern.

nonCodeExtensions..json: static data (e.g. translation files), never imports code
